title: Distributed Systems & Raft Consensus Implementation (PYTH_183_S1 to PYTH_183_S8)

slides.title: Raft Consensus Algorithm
slides.prompt: Raft achieves distributed consensus across a cluster of nodes using leader election, log replication, and term monotonicity.
slides.codeSnippet:
# Raft Node State Concept
class NodeState(Enum):
    FOLLOWER = 1
    CANDIDATE = 2
    LEADER = 3

slides.title: Raft Monotonic Terms
slides.prompt: Fill in the state property term used by Raft nodes to track election epochs sequentially.

slides.title: Leader Election Trigger
slides.prompt: What causes a Raft follower node to transition into the Candidate state and initiate a new leader election?
options: Elapsing of the randomized election timeout without receiving heartbeats from a valid leader
Receiving an explicit shutdown command from an administrator
Filling up the node's local disk log storage
Detecting a network socket port conflict
slides.correctAnswer: Elapsing of the randomized election timeout without receiving heartbeats from a valid leader

slides.title: Heartbeat Communication
slides.prompt: Fill in the Raft RPC command sent periodically by the leader to suppress follower election timeouts.

slides.title: Quorum Majority Requirement
slides.prompt: How many vote approvals does a Candidate node require to safely win an election in a 5-node cluster?

slides.title: Vote Request RPC
slides.prompt: Fill in the Raft RPC name invoked by Candidates to collect votes during elections.

slides.title: Log Commit Safety Condition
slides.prompt: When is a log entry safely considered 'committed' in a Raft cluster?
options: When it has been replicated onto a majority of cluster node logs by the leader of the current term
As soon as the client submits the request to the network interface
When all follower nodes flush their memory cache to disk
slides.correctAnswer: When it has been replicated onto a majority of cluster node logs by the leader of the current term

slides.title: State Machine Application
slides.prompt: Fill in the index tracking variable used to mark log entries applied to the local state machine.
